name: preempt-rt

change.description: Apply the exact Linux 5.15.211-rt97 patch and enable CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT, retaining the physical TIM3/PB4-to-PG7 scope contract.

constant_contract.kernel: Linux 5.15.211-rt97 ARM NOMMU FDPIC XIP from QSPI
constant_contract.data: VFAT on the same SD card at approximately 1.95 MHz
constant_contract.latency: TIM3 CH1 PB4/D3 hardware reference to priority-99 SCHED_FIFO kthread PG7/D4 response

required_rt_fixes: Use raw_spinlock_t for rt_scope state shared with the IRQF_NO_THREAD TIM3 interrupt.
Run the non-DMA STM32 USART handler as an explicit IRQ thread on PREEMPT_RT.

idle_scope_sample.note: Idle diagnostic only; it is not comparable to a loaded 300-second hammer scope sample.

failures.symptom: FDPIC NOMMU allocation of 520192 bytes failed at order 7 after PREEMPT_RT required the SLUB allocator.
The forced-thread MMCI path returned repeated single-sector write I/O errors; the existing bounded polling workaround depended on hard-IRQ timing.

fat_recovery.conclusion: The on-disk structures were readable after repair, but repeated block write errors make this kernel unsuitable for a full hammer result.

decision: Do not report a throughput comparison for this iteration. Preserve PREEMPT_RT and the boot fixes, reduce the SQLite static heap below a NOMMU order-6 allocation, and repair the MMCI write timing in a separately committed iteration before rerunning hammer.
interpretation: PREEMPT_RT boots cleanly and the idle missed-release rate is below one percent, but that sample is unloaded. The failed smoke demonstrates that allocator and driver execution-context changes are part of the cost of adopting PREEMPT_RT on this 8 MiB NOMMU target; a valid loaded comparison does not yet exist.
